summary: Resolve grid, socket or angle candidates into a reversible preview before one explicit legal placement is committed.
objective: The preview explains which target and orientation will win, while cancellation, invalid placement and camera movement leave committed state untouched.
applies_when: A dragged or stepped object may align to authored increments, sockets, surfaces or orientations.
intent_signals: show a ghost before snapping the module
two sockets compete near a corner
invalid snap must not enter undo
example_prompts: Preview which equipment socket will receive the dragged module, then commit on release.
Snap a puzzle piece to legal cells without moving it when the drag is cancelled.
not_for: Continuous free manipulation with no discrete target.

principles: A snap candidate combines a semantic target, compatible role, pose and validity result; distance alone does not establish compatibility.
Preview state is derived and disposable. It may show a ghost, guide, target highlight and rejection reason without mutating occupancy, hierarchy or undo history.
Choose deterministic candidate ranking and tie-breaking, and declare entry and exit behavior so small pointer noise does not make the preview flicker between targets.
Commit revalidates against current authoritative state because another edit may have changed occupancy or permission after the preview was calculated.
implementation: Author grid increments, socket frames, compatibility keys and keep-out guides in Blender or application data; export stable identities rather than assuming proximity carries meaning.
Generate candidates in one declared coordinate frame. Rank only compatible candidates using authored priorities and geometric distance or angle, with a stable ID tie-break.
Render the winning preview separately from committed geometry. Preserve the original parent and local transform until release or explicit Commit.

On commit, recheck target existence, compatibility, occupancy, transform limits and permissions; write placement and occupancy atomically as one command. Invalid, cancelled and pre-commit capture-loss attempts create no command.
Provide discrete target-next, rotate-step and Place/Cancel actions where the spatial drag is essential to the task.
observable_checks: Approach two equally near sockets repeatedly; the declared tie-break chooses the same candidate and the preview does not alternate under small motion.
Invalidate or occupy the previewed target before release; commit rejects or recomputes according to policy without leaving half-updated occupancy or transforms.
Cancel from valid and invalid previews; committed parent, transform, occupancy and history remain byte-for-byte or structurally equal to the start state.
A nested, rotated module commits the same world pose shown by the preview after conversion back to its chosen parent frame.

creative_affordances: Use magnetic arcs, projected footprints or animated socket rings to make target ownership readable.
Let rejected candidates explain collision, role or occupancy with shape and text rather than color alone.
known_limits: No universal snap radius, hysteresis band or priority order is prescribed.
Authoring-time Blender snapping and runtime application snapping are separate systems.
Authored and source-checked guidance; no placement runtime was executed.

claims.statement: Blender 4.5 documents separate snap-base and snap-target choices, including increment or grid and geometric targets such as vertex, edge and face, and allows snapping to affect move, rotate and scale operations.
claims.scope: Blender authoring controls only; they do not define runtime compatibility, candidate ranking or atomic placement.

source_refs.locator: Snap Base; Snap Target; Affect; Rotation Increment

claims.statement: Current Three.js TransformControls documents translation snapping as numeric world-unit steps and rotation snapping as numeric radian steps, with null defaults for continuous transformation.
claims.scope: Current addon properties; the documentation does not supply socket compatibility, preview hysteresis or commit validation.
